Adding tools and MCP servers to Java AI agents with Embabel
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on walkthrough of building a Java AI blog-writing agent using the Embabel framework on the JVM. Covers adding custom tools (a reading stats calculator), integrating MCP servers (Brave web search), using built-in tool groups for web research, and configuring logging personalities. The agent is extended step-by-step from two actions to a full pipeline that researches topics, writes drafts, adds TL;DR summaries, and generates front matter with reading time estimates.

recent_posts.title: Building AI Agents in Java with Embabel (Getting Started)
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on getting started tutorial for Embabel, a JVM framework for building AI agents created by Rod Johnson (founder of Spring Framework). Covers core concepts including goal-oriented action planning (GOAP), actions, goals, and plans. Walks through building a blog-writing agent from scratch using Spring Boot 3.5, demonstrating type-safe domain models with Java records, multi-model configuration (GPT-4o-mini for drafting, GPT-4o for reviewing), personas as reusable prompt contributors, and writing output to markdown files. Also shows the shell interface for inspecting agents, listing models, and debugging LLM interactions with verbose output.

recent_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 09 - Observability
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial on adding observability to GraphQL applications built with Spring for GraphQL and Spring Boot 4. Covers the three pillars of observability (logging, metrics, traces) and demonstrates how to use the new Spring Boot Starter OpenTelemetry to get production-ready instrumentation with minimal setup. Shows how to configure trace sampling probability, use the LGTM stack (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir) via Docker Compose, and visualize GraphQL query traces and metrics in Grafana to identify performance bottlenecks in data-fetching operations.

recent_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 07 - Data Integration (GraphQLRepository + AOT Repositories)
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial covering two Spring Data features for GraphQL Java APIs: the @GraphQLRepository annotation and AOT repositories. The @GraphQLRepository annotation automatically generates data fetchers and enables dynamic query-by-example filtering without writing controllers or individual data fetcher mappings. AOT repositories, enabled via a Maven plugin, shift Spring Data repository implementation generation from runtime to compile time, yielding 50-70% startup improvements in larger applications and making generated SQL queries visible and debuggable. Both features work with Spring Data JPA and JDBC.

recent_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 08 - Client Integration with HttpSyncGraphQlClient
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of using Spring for GraphQL's HttpSyncGraphQlClient to consume a GraphQL API from a Java client application. The tutorial covers setting up a standalone Spring Boot app with WebApplicationType.NONE, building the client using RestClient.Builder, writing document-based queries with variables, and mapping responses to entity classes using toEntity(). It also touches on the async alternative (retrieveSync vs retrieve with WebFlux), storing queries in resource files, and using the client for integration testing.

recent_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 10 - Course Conclusion and Next Steps
recent_posts.summary: Conclusion of a full GraphQL for Java developers course, summarizing key topics covered including schema-first design, building GraphQL APIs with Spring for GraphQL, and when to use GraphQL over REST. Recommends next steps such as building your own API, exploring GraphQL Federation, and points to additional resources including official docs, GraphQL Java docs, and graphql.org.

recent_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 06 - N+1 Problem and Virtual Threads
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on tutorial covering two key GraphQL performance problems in Java: the N+1 problem and sequential execution. The N+1 issue arises when fetching books for each author triggers a separate call per author. The solution uses Spring for GraphQL's @BatchMapping annotation to batch all author IDs into a single query. Virtual threads (enabled via a single property) are also introduced to parallelize field resolver calls, reducing multi-second sequential delays to near-instant responses.

recent_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 05 - Unions
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of GraphQL unions in the context of Java and Spring for GraphQL. Covers how to declare a union type in a GraphQL schema (e.g., SearchItem as either Author or Book), implement a search query controller that queries multiple repositories, and use the inline fragment syntax (... on TypeName) in GraphQL queries to request type-specific fields. Also demonstrates the __typename meta-field for identifying returned types at runtime.

recent_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 04 - Data Fetchers
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial on implementing GraphQL data fetchers in Java using Spring for GraphQL. Covers creating a controller with @QueryMapping and @SchemaMapping annotations to bind schema fields to Java methods, using the GraphiQL explorer to test queries, handling arguments with @Argument, defining input types vs output types, and implementing a mutation to add new records. Demonstrates querying a list of books, fetching a single book by ID, and adding a book via mutation with a BookInput record.

top_posts.title: Building a Terminal UI for Spring Initializr with Java
top_posts.summary: A developer built a terminal UI (TUI) for Spring Initializr using Java and the newly announced Tamboo UI framework. The tool replicates the Spring Initializr web experience in the terminal, with features like fuzzy dependency search, favorites, project exploration, and post-generation hooks that can automatically open an IDE (like IntelliJ) and launch Claude Code in the new project directory. The native executable is built with GraalVM for fast startup and low memory usage, and binaries for macOS, Windows, and Linux are distributed via GitHub releases.

top_posts.title: JDK 26: Final Will Actually Mean Final Now
top_posts.summary: JDK 26 introduces JEP 500 'Prepare to Make Final Mean Final', the first step in the 'Integrity by Default' initiative. Currently, Java's final fields can be mutated via deep reflection using setAccessible(true). In JDK 26, this behavior now triggers a warning by default, with optional debug and deny modes configurable via the --illegal-final-field-mutation JVM flag. A hands-on demo shows the mutation working silently in JDK 25, then producing warnings in JDK 26, and throwing an IllegalAccessException in deny mode. Full enforcement blocking final field mutation via reflection is planned for a future JDK release.

top_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 03 - The GraphQL Schema
top_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of the schema-first approach in GraphQL for Java developers using Spring for GraphQL. Covers creating a .graphqls schema file, defining object types (Book and Author) with scalar types and non-null constraints, and introducing operation types (query, mutation, subscription). Also demonstrates Spring for GraphQL's schema mapping inspection report, which highlights unmapped fields and other schema issues at startup.

top_posts.title: Spring Boot RestClient Error Handling
top_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough of best practices for error handling with Spring Boot's RestClient. Key tips include: using the default RestClient builder for built-in observability, centralizing error handling via a default status handler at the client configuration level instead of per-method, defining custom exceptions (e.g., NotFoundException, ApiException), using @RestControllerAdvice with ProblemDetail (RFC 9457) for structured error responses, and leveraging the @Retryable annotation with exponential backoff from Spring Framework 7's built-in resilience methods. The demo uses httpbin.org to simulate various HTTP status codes and Spring Boot 4 with JDK 26.

top_posts.title: GraphQL for Java Developers: 04 - Data Fetchers
top_posts.summary: A tutorial on implementing GraphQL data fetchers in Java using Spring for GraphQL. Covers creating a controller with @QueryMapping and @SchemaMapping annotations to bind schema fields to Java methods, using the GraphiQL explorer to test queries, handling arguments with @Argument, defining input types vs output types, and implementing a mutation to add new records. Demonstrates querying a list of books, fetching a single book by ID, and adding a book via mutation with a BookInput record.
